subtopics.title: International Affairs and Places
subtopics.summary: This group covers a three-nation defence pact in West Asia, the NATO Ankara Summit 2026, the India-Bangladesh Ganga water sharing treaty and Nauru's new indigenous name. The pact and the summit both concern collective defence, while the treaty and the renaming concern shared resources and national identity.
facts: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement.
Türkiye described the pact as a defence-oriented partnership, not an alliance aimed at a particular country.
An armed attack on one member is to be treated as an attack on all three.
The pact is meant to complement existing regional and international security mechanisms rather than replace them.
The 2025 Pakistan-Saudi Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement was expanded into a trilateral framework.
NATO Ankara Summit 2026 followed the 2025 Hague Summit.
NATO members endorsed the Hague Defence Commitment to spend 5% of GDP on defence by 2035.
The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is scheduled to expire in December 2026.
The Farakka Barrage is on the Ganga river at Murshidabad, West Bengal.
Nauru adopted the indigenous name Republic of Naoero to strengthen cultural identity and sovereignty.

subtopics.title: Governance, Welfare and Digital Safety
subtopics.summary: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill 2026 would change ISI's legal status and governance, with the President of India as Visitor. The NCDC (Amendment) Bill 2026 widens direct financing for cooperatives, and PM-VBRY supports first-time employment. Meta's new teen safety rules follow a settlement with 52 State Attorneys General.
facts: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill 2026 was introduced in Lok Sabha and seeks to repeal the ISI Act, 1959.
Under the Bill, the President of India would become the Visitor of the Indian Statistical Institute.
The Visitor can review functioning, order inquiries and issue binding directions.
The existing 33-member Council would be replaced by an 11-member Board of Governors.
The Director would be appointed by the Board with the Visitor's prior approval and would act as chief executive officer.
Under the Bill, central approval would be required only for the first set of regulations.
Parliament passed the National Cooperative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
NCDC can now lend or grant funds directly to any cooperative society, subject to prescribed conditions.
PM-VBRY completed one year, and its implementation period runs from 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027.
Meta plans default safety limits for teens, including a 2-hour cumulative daily limit across Instagram and Facebook.

subtopics.title: Environment, Energy and Wildlife
subtopics.summary: This group covers elephant and lion conservation, India's low rank in the Environmental Performance Index 2026, and two clean-energy schemes. The wildlife items show conservation efforts, while the index and the energy schemes show how environmental goals are being pursued.
facts: India observed World Elephant Day on 12 August 2026 with the theme 'Bringing the World together to help Elephants'.
A Rs 2,500 crore regional action plan covers Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.
Phase II of the Human-Elephant Conflict study covers Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and West Bengal.
India has 33 Elephant Reserves and 150 identified elephant corridors.
The synchronous estimation for 2021-25 put India's wild elephant population at 22,446.
Project Lion was launched on 15 August 2020.
The Asiatic lion population rose from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025.
India ranked 176th of 177 countries in the Environmental Performance Index 2026, and Estonia topped the index.
The Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park is on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh.
GOBARdhan converts animal waste, crop residue and kitchen waste into compressed biogas and bio-slurry.

subtopics.title: History, Symbols and Personalities
subtopics.summary: This group covers P.C. Mahalanobis and National Statistics Day, the national flag and the role of Pingali Venkayya, and the 1946 Royal Indian Navy Mutiny. The items link science, national symbols and anti-colonial protest. Venkayya's 150th birth anniversary was marked in 2026.
facts: P.C. Mahalanobis is regarded as the Father of Indian Statistics.
He founded Sankhya, India's first statistical journal, in 1933.
He drafted India's 2nd Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), based on his four-sector model.
India designated 29 June as National Statistics Day in 2007.
The 2026 theme of National Statistics Day is 'Unlocking Potential of Administrative Data'.
Pingali Venkayya was born on 2 August 1876 in Krishna, Andhra Pradesh.
In 1921, Venkayya presented a khadi flag design to Mahatma Gandhi at the Congress session in Vijayawada.
The white band on the flag represents peace and truth, and the Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes.
The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny began at HMIS Talwar in Bombay on 18 February 1946.
Rebels in the mutiny organised under a Naval Strike Committee.

subtopics.title: Awards, Science and Agriculture
subtopics.summary: This group covers the Fields Medal 2026, the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal 2026 and India's new popcorn maize hybrid. The award items explain eligibility, frequency and awarding bodies, while the maize item places the crop among India's major food crops.
facts: The Fields Medal 2026 was awarded to Yu Deng, John Pardon, Jacob Tsimerman and Hong Wang.
Hong Wang became the third woman to win the Fields Medal.
The Fields Medal was established in 1936 through the efforts of John Charles Fields.
Fields Medal recipients must be below 40 years of age at the time of the award.
Two to four mathematicians may be honoured in each cycle, and the medal is awarded once every four years.
The Fields Medal is awarded by the International Mathematical Union.
Annapurni Subramaniam, Director of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, Bengaluru, received the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal 2026.
The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal was established in 1990 and is awarded biennially.
The medal was conferred at the 46th Scientific Assembly in Florence, Italy.
India's indigenous, non-GMO popcorn maize hybrid seed was launched at Musunuru, Eluru, Andhra Pradesh.

quizzes.title: Flag, freedom and the navy
quizzes.passage:
The national flag of India took shape over several decades of the freedom struggle. Pingali Venkayya, a freedom fighter from Andhra Pradesh, worked on flag designs and is remembered for his role in the Indian Tricolour. At the 1921 session of the Indian National Congress held at Vijayawada, he presented a khadi flag design to Mahatma Gandhi. His first design had red and green bands, with a charkha at the centre, representing the two major communities. On Gandhi's suggestion, a white band was added to stand for peace, while the charkha was kept as a symbol of self-reliance. In 1931, the Congress formally adopted a modified tricolour, which became the precursor of the present flag. The Constituent Assembly adopted the present National Flag on 22 July 1947, and it became the national flag of independent India on 15 August 1947.

The freedom movement also reached the armed forces. In 1946, Indian naval ratings rose against British authorities in several port cities, demanding better food, pay comparable with the Royal Navy, and an end to the use of Indian personnel for British imperial expansion. The uprising drew support from workers, students and civilians. Its anti-colonial mood was shaped in part by the legacy of the Indian National Army trials.

Symbols and protests of this period show how closely ideas of unity, peace and self-reliance were linked with the struggle for independence.

questions.q: On which date did the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of 1946 begin at HMIS Talwar in Bombay?
questions.explanation: The uprising began at HMIS Talwar in Bombay on 18 February 1946.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution mandates respect for the national flag and anthem?
questions.explanation: Article 51A(a) mandates respect for the flag and anthem.

questions.q: How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra on the national flag have?
questions.explanation: The Ashoka Chakra is a navy blue wheel with 24 spokes.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The white band on the national flag represents peace and truth.
Reason (R): Flag or anthem offences lead to a 6-year election ban under the National Honour Act.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the election ban under the National Honour Act does not explain the meaning of the white band.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Ashoka Chakra   ->   C. Navy blue wheel with 24 spokes
II. Green colour on the flag   ->   A. Fertility and growth
III. First flag hoisted in Kolkata (1907)   ->   D. Red, yellow and green stripes with Vande Mataram
IV. Flag Code of India   ->   B. Governs display and use of the flag
questions.explanation: The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes, green denotes fertility and growth, the 1907 Kolkata flag had Vande Mataram, and the Flag Code governs display and use.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Venkayya met Mahatma Gandhi during the 2nd Boer War (1899-1902).
II. Venkayya authored The Mother of Diamonds in 1921.
III. All India Radio Vijayawada was renamed in his honour in 2015.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because The Mother of Diamonds was authored in 1955, not 1921.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of 1946:
I. It spread to Karachi, Visakhapatnam, Jamnagar and Kolkata.
II. Rebels organised themselves under a Naval Strike Committee.
III. One of its demands was the withdrawal of British Indian troops from Indonesia.
IV. It began at HMIS Talwar in Karachi.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I, II and III are correct, while IV is wrong because the mutiny began at HMIS Talwar in Bombay.

questions.q: The Royal Indian Navy Mutiny of 1946 was partly shaped by the legacy of the INA trials and which leader?
questions.explanation: The INA trials and the legacy of Subhas Chandra Bose strengthened anti-British sentiment among naval ratings.

quizzes.title: Wildlife, index and energy
quizzes.passage:
India's environment and energy policies in 2026 covered wildlife, waste and clean power. India observed World Elephant Day on 12 August, when new initiatives were announced for elephant conservation, including a regional action plan for southern states and a model conservation plan for the Nilgiri Elephant Reserve. Elephants are the largest land animals on Earth, and their conservation depends on reducing conflict with people. Scientists and officials use population studies and monitoring programmes to plan protection of the animals and their migratory routes. Lions also drew attention through Project Lion, which marked a rise in the Asiatic lion population and used software for individual identification of the animals.

On the environment front, India remained among the lowest-performing countries in the Environmental Performance Index, a biennial assessment of 177 countries. The index tracks environmental health, ecosystem vitality and climate change as its main policy objectives. Its air quality and biodiversity ranks were among the weakest, though climate change and sanitation showed some improvement.

For energy, the Cabinet approved a scheme to expand floating solar power linked with energy storage, to strengthen grid stability. The floating solar projects are a central sector scheme targeting 5,000 MW of capacity. A separate scheme, GOBARdhan, aims to convert organic waste into compressed biogas and bio-slurry. Together, these measures show how waste management and clean energy are being linked with the country's environmental goals.

questions.q: What was the estimated wild elephant population of India in the 2021-25 synchronous estimation? (in number)
questions.explanation: The synchronous All India Population Estimation (2021-25) put India's wild elephant population at 22,446.

questions.q: What rank did India get among 177 countries in the Environmental Performance Index 2026? (rank number)
questions.explanation: India ranked 176th of 177 countries in the Environmental Performance Index 2026.

questions.q: What was the Asiatic lion population in 2025? (in number)
questions.explanation: The Asiatic lion population rose from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025.

questions.q: Which country topped the Environmental Performance Index 2026?
questions.explanation: Estonia topped the Environmental Performance Index 2026, while India ranked 176th.

questions.q: In which year was the Gir Wildlife Sanctuary established?
questions.explanation: Gir Wildlife Sanctuary was established in 1965.

questions.q: On which river is the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park located?
questions.explanation: The Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park is located on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: How many Elephant Reserves does India have? (in number)
questions.explanation: India has 33 Elephant Reserves and 150 identified elephant corridors.
